# 1 Clement Chapter 18 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 18 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_018_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 18

**18:1** But what shall we say about David, to whom testimony was borne, and of whom God said: "I have found a man after my own heart, David the son of Jesse; I have anointed him with eternal mercy." [Ps 89:20; 1 Sam 13:14; Acts 13:22]

**18:2** But even he says to God: "Have mercy upon me, O God, according to your great mercy; and according to the multitude of your compassions, blot out my transgression.

**18:3** Wash me yet more from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin. For I acknowledge my iniquity, and my sin is before me always.

**18:4** Against you only have I sinned, and done that which is evil in your sight; that you may be justified in your words and may conquer when you are judged.

**18:5** For behold, I was conceived in iniquities, and in sins my mother bore me.

**18:6** For behold, you have loved truth; the hidden and secret things of your wisdom you have made manifest to me.

**18:7** You shall sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be clean; you shall wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.

**18:8** You shall make me to hear joy and gladness; the bones that have been humbled shall rejoice.

**18:9** Turn away your face from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities.

**18:10** Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.

**18:11** Cast me not away from your presence, and take not your holy spirit from me.

**18:12** Restore unto me the joy of your salvation, and strengthen me with a governing spirit.

**18:13** I will teach transgressors your ways, and the ungodly shall be converted unto you.

**18:14** Deliver me from blood-guiltiness, O God, the God of my salvation; my tongue shall exult in your righteousness.

**18:15** Lord, you shall open my mouth, and my lips shall declare your praise.

**18:16** For if you had desired sacrifice, I would have given it; with burnt-offerings you will not be pleased.

**18:17** A sacrifice to God is a broken spirit; a broken and humbled heart God will not despise." [Ps 51:1-17 LXX]

---

*EMET: The full Psalm 51 (LXX 50) — the Miserere — is here cited as the greatest expression of humility. David, the man after God's heart, is Clement's supreme example of humble confession. The citation is near-complete and close to the LXX text.*
